title: WISDOM Project - XIII. Feeding molecular gas to the supermassive black hole in the starburst AGN-host galaxy Fairall 49
question: What is the supermassive black hole mass, molecular gas mass, CO-to-H2 conversion factor, and gas inflow rate in the starburst AGN-host galaxy Fairall 49 using high-resolution ALMA CO(2-1) kinematics?

data.sensitivity: 0.038 mJy/beam (continuum); 0.7 mJy/beam per 15 km/s channel (CO cube mean rms); 0.84 mJy/beam (PV diagram rms)

what.value: Redshift z = 0.02002 and line-of-sight velocity 6002 km/s

evidence.loc: The target: a LIRG with a Seyfert nucleus
evidence.quote: Considering that Fairall 49 has a line-of-sight velocity of 6002 $\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$(cite: Huchra2012), we obtain $D = 86.7$ Mpc, so 1$''$ corresponds to $\sim$0.42 kpc.

what.value: Total far-IR luminosity L_FIR = 1.1 x 10^11 L_odot
SMBH and stellar mass data for 83 ETGs, six WISDOM ETGs, and NGC 404 for the M_BH - M_star scaling relation fit

evidence.loc: Implications for the SMBH and host galaxy
evidence.quote: To investigate the location of Fairall 49 on the $M_\bullet-M_\star$ relation, we consider the data from (cite: Sahu2019) for 83 ETGs and update them with six SMBH measurements from WISDOM (cite: WISDOM-1; WISDOM-2; WISDOM-3; WISDOM-4; WISDOM-5; WISDOM-7).

evidence.loc: Implications for the SMBH and host galaxy
evidence.quote: We also add the dwarf lenticular galaxy NGC 404 (cite: Davis2020) as well as Fairall 49.

external_data.citation: (cite: Sahu2019; WISDOM-1; WISDOM-2; WISDOM-3; WISDOM-4; WISDOM-5; WISDOM-7; Davis2020)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA Band 6 continuum and CO(2-1) line datacube
recipe.method: Calibrate uv data with CASA pipeline, manually flag bad antennas/baselines with flagdata, image continuum with tclean, subtract continuum in uv plane with uvcontsub (1st-order polynomial), bin to 15 km/s, clean cube with CASA tclean and GIPSY clean, and extract moment maps with 3DBAROLO
key_parameters: Högbom deconvolver, Briggs robust = 0.5, cleaned down to ~3 sigma, 15 km/s channel binning, GIPSY Boolean mask smoothed to 0.4'' clipped at 3 sigma_s

recipe.goal: Extract HST F606W surface photometry and calculate the stellar gravitational potential
recipe.method: Fit ellipses to HST WFPC2 F606W isophotes using ARCHANGEL to derive the 1D surface brightness profile; non-parametrically subtract the inner HSB (AGN/starburst) component within R_HSB ~ 200 pc; compute stellar circular velocity contribution using both 1D MGE (MGEFIT) and thick-disk (GIPSY Rotmod) methods
key_parameters: 1D MGE axial ratio q = 0.01; thick-disk exponential vertical scale height h_z = 253 pc; baseline HSB subtraction of ~10^9 L_odot within ~200 pc
assumptions: Inner HSB component within ~200 pc is dominated by AGN and starburst emission rather than tracing stellar mass (assigned M/L = 0 in baseline model)
Thick-disk vertical scale height h_z = 253 pc from empirical relation h_z = 0.196 h_R^0.633 with h_R ~ 1.5 kpc

recipe.goal: Fit 3D tilted-ring kinematic model to the CO(2-1) datacube
recipe.method: Divide the CO disk into 19 independent concentric rings and perform a two-stage 3D tilted-ring fit with 3DBAROLO to derive rotation velocity, radial velocity, and velocity dispersion profiles
key_parameters: 19 rings of width 0.186'' (out to ~3.5''), cos(theta) azimuthal weighting, exponential vertical profile with z_0 = 100 pc (0.25''), twostage=true, polyn=0
assumptions: Fully axisymmetric flat gas disk with exponential vertical distribution (scale height 100 pc); western side is near side based on HST dust lanes

recipe.goal: Fit dynamical mass models to the rotation curve and derive gas inflow rate
recipe.method: Fit a 4-component mass model (stellar disk, molecular gas disk, central SMBH, NFW dark matter halo) to the 3DBAROLO rotation curve using MCMC (emcee), and compute radial gas inflow rate Mdot_gas(R) = M_gas(R) * V_rad(R) / R
key_parameters: 200 walkers, 1000 burn-in iterations, 2000 sampling iterations, stretch move parameter a = 2, gas vertical scale height h_z = 100 pc
assumptions: Molecular gas is in dynamical equilibrium; atomic gas (HI) contribution is neglected; D = 86.7 Mpc, H_0 = 75 km/s/Mpc; spherical NFW DM halo obeying Moster+2013 and Dutton+2014 scaling relations

recipe.goal: Forward model the inner CO(2-1) datacube directly with KINMS
recipe.method: Fit a 12-parameter global dynamical model directly to the inner CO datacube (R <= 1'') using KINMS in an MCMC framework
key_parameters: Fitted region R <= 1'' (and R < 0.5'' test), 12 free parameters, 30000 MCMC samples, fixed Upsilon_gas, V_200, and C_200 from full rotation-curve fit
assumptions: Exponential CO surface brightness profile exp(-R/R_gas) and linear radial velocity trend V_rad,0 * (1 - R/R_Vrad)

recipe.goal: Fit the M_BH - M_star scaling relation and evaluate X_CO and R_21
recipe.method: Fit linear scaling relation to SMBH and stellar masses of ETGs + WISDOM sample + Fairall 49 using BayesLineFit; compare dynamical gas mass to CO-luminosity-based gas mass under Galactic and starburst X_CO and R_21 assumptions
key_parameters: Milky Way X_CO,20 = 2, thermalized R_21 = 1, Helium correction factor 1.37; starburst X_CO,20 = 0.2 and Seyfert R_21 = 2.5

evidence.quote: For large line-of-sight velocities, the effect of peculiar velocities on $D$ is not large, so the distance uncertainty is plausibly of the order of 10$\%$.
For our baseline model, the luminosity of the HSB component is about $10^9$ L$_\odot$ within $\sim$200 pc ($\sim$0.5$''$), corresponding to 8$\%$ of the total luminosity of Fairall 49.

(2) The dynamically inferred SMBH mass is $1.6\pm0.4\mathrm{(rnd)}\pm0.8 \mathrm{(sys)}\times 10^{8}$ $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ assuming that we have accurately subtracted the AGN and starburst light contributions, which have a luminosity of $\sim$10$^9$ L$_\odot$;
To explain the inner parts of the rotation curve, the mass model requires a central SMBH with a mass of $1.6 \pm 0.4 (\mathrm{rnd}) \pm 0.8 (\mathrm{sys}) \times 10^{8}$ $M_\odot$

For the baseline mass model in Figure 1, the SOI of the SMBH occurs at $R\simeq150$ pc (within which $V_\bullet > V_\star$), so it is well resolved by the angular resolution of the ALMA data ($\sim$80 pc).
while the rotation-curve fit (Sect. 0.1) gives $\Upsilon_\star=1.8\pm0.1$ and $M_\bullet = (1.6 \pm 0.4) \times 10^8$ M$_\odot$

score_reason: Both the ALMA data (2017.1.00904.S) and HST WFPC2 data (ID 5479) are public in archives, all software packages (CASA, GIPSY, 3DBAROLO, KINMS, ARCHANGEL, MGEFIT, emcee, BayesLineFit) are publicly available, and the MCMC priors, ring parameters, and dynamical equations are thoroughly specified, with only minor imaging parameters (cell size, exact manual flags) and the tabulated 1D subtracted light profile omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA and HST data with a clear, well-documented two-pronged dynamical modeling recipe (3DBAROLO + emcee and KINMS) yielding concrete numeric targets for SMBH mass, stellar mass, gas mass, and radial inflow velocity.
